title: Glory be to You, O Allah
cue: The opening praise Umar said aloud to teach it
arabic: سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ
transliteration: Subhaanakallaahumma wabihamdik, tabaarakasmuka wata'aalaa jadduk, walaa ilaha ghayruk
translation: Glory be to You, O Allah, with Your praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted Your majesty, and there is no god but You.

gradings.in: Sahih Muslim, no. 399, as Umar's own practice

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sahih Muslim, ed. Muhammad Fu’ad Abd al-Baqi, hadith 399: https://shamela.ws/book/1727/835

usage.evidence: Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say these words aloud [at the start of the prayer] (Muslim 399). It is cited here as Umar's practice. Al-Tirmidhi also relates it from the Prophet ﷺ (242, 243), says the chains of both narrations were criticised, and says most of the people of knowledge act on it.
